request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree search is in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

There's a search box (`search-name`) and a Search button (`search`). Pressing it lists every person on this sheet and on the other sheets of its tree whose name or an alias contains the typed text, ignoring case. Each line (`search-line`) reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`, and `search-count` shows how many lines there are. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people by sheet id. An empty search lists everyone.

**What I added:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree`, returns the other sheets of the tree: the sheet's ancestors, then its descendants, counting only sheets that exist. It reuses the same tree definition the app already uses for name clashes.
- **Screen:** a new panel in `features/search/search.slot.tsx`. It reads each sheet's people and computes their due-totals the same way their rows on the people list do, so "n/a" appears where the person list shows it. It follows the same pattern as the existing consolidated header figures.

**Choices the request left open:**
- **Retired people are included,** even when "show retired" is off, because the request says "every person".
- **Searches show the sheets as they are now,** even if the screen is set to an earlier as-of date. The consolidated figures behave the same way. The tests never search under an as-of date, so this is untested.
- **Old results disappear on each press:** the count and lines are cleared, the tree and the other sheets' data are re-read, and the count only reappears once every sheet has loaded.
- **Sibling sheets are left out.** "Tree" means ancestors and descendants, not the whole tree from the top sheet down.

The search doesn't change any data, so it writes nothing to the audit file.

probe.probe_text:
I've read enough to answer: the claim, person, rollup, statement, period, setting, rate and role code on the server, and the feature slots on the front end. I changed nothing. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## A claim's row (`features/claims/list.slot.tsx`) **Shown as stored:** `claim-number`, `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-ref`, `claim-tags`, `claim-status`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-stated`, `claim-deferred-until`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-batch`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-proofs`, plus the log, comment and line lists. **Worked out:** - **`claim-due`** comes from `claimDue()` in `rates.ts`. The same logic exists in Java as `ClaimFigure.of` + `Lateness.due`. 1. If the claim has a `settledDue`, that is the due. It was frozen when settled, with the late charge and floor already in it. 2. Otherwise, if the claim `isBound` (`stated` and `statedDue`/`statedNa` set, and not PENDING), the due starts from the `statedDue` figure, which is n/a when `statedNa`. 3. Otherwise the figure is amount × the rate ÷ 100, to 2 decimals. The rate is the one in force on the claim's date (`rateOf`/`RateStore.find`) for the grade in force on that date (`gradeOn`). If the sheet has no such rate, it walks up to 3 `parent` sheets. If the rate's `to` date is before the claim date, or there is no rate, the figure is n/a. 4. **Rounding** (`Rounding`): half up if `roundsBy` is before the policy date (the `policy-date` setting, else the sheet's today), half even otherwise. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. 5. **Late charge** (`Lateness.charge` / `lateCharge`): only for OPEN or PENDING claims that are not corrections and not deferred. It counts from `graceBy`, which is `dueBy` plus the grace days in force for the person's grade on the claim's date. For each full 30 days past that, it adds the `late-pct` in force on that boundary date, applied to the figure plus the earlier charges, so it compounds. Each step is rounded the same way. A statement never binds the charge. 6. **Floor** (`floored`/`liveDue`): applied last. It is the floor in force on the claim's date, defaulting to 1.00. Corrections get no floor. - **`claim-due-by`**: fixed when the claim is added as the Nth business day after its date, skipping weekends and holidays (`HolidayStore.businessDaysAfter`). N is the person's own `terms`, else their grade's `terms-X` on that date, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14) (`SaveClaimAdded.termsOf`). - Editing, re-dating or reassigning the claim leaves it unchanged. - Adding a holiday re-fixes it for every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday (`refixDueBy`, using the stored `due_terms`). - **`claim-overdue`**: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `graceBy` is before today. - **`claim-period`**: the period that contains `dueBy`, not the claim's date (`ClaimPeriods`). - **`claim-deferred`**: the status is OPEN (or VOID, for display only) and today is before `deferredUntil` (`ClaimResponse.on`). - **`claim-number`** (`Numbering`): given only when the claim is opened. - If `period-numbering-from` is set and today is on or after it, the number is `-n`, or `X-n` when `dueBy` falls in no period. - Otherwise it is `FY-n`, counted per fiscal year of `dueBy` (using `fiscal-start-month`) and shared across the whole sheet tree. - A voided claim keeps its number. Reassigning or transferring a claim gives it a new number. ## A person's row (one slot per column) - **`person-claimed`**: the sum of the amounts of claims that count, excluding claims that correct another. - **`person-due-total`**: `personDue`, the sum of the dues of claims that count, capped at `cap`. - It is n/a when the person's grade today has no rate today, unless a counting claim is settled or stated, or has a figure at another grade or at a rate that has ended. - n/a is never capped. - **`person-excess`**: the uncapped total minus `cap`, or 0.00. - **`person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`**: the uncapped total split into SETTLED and OPEN+PENDING claims. Both are 0.00 when the total is n/a. - **`person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`**: the count and sum of dues of counting claims that are overdue. - **`person-aged-0-30` / `-31-60` / `-61`**: dues of counting OPEN/PENDING claims, bucketed by days since the claim's date. A future date counts as 0. - **`person-period-

-due-total`**: if the period is closed or soft-closed, the figure fixed at that time. Otherwise, the sum of claims whose `dueBy` is in the period and that count by their status at the period's end (taken from the log), using the live counting rules. - **`person-active`**: has a counting OPEN/PENDING claim dated in the last 30 days. - **`person-backing`**: patron shares are 100 ÷ n, rounded half even, with the remainder going to the first patron. Each patron's figure is the sum of their SETTLED claims' frozen dues dated in the last 90 days. The backing is figure × share, summed and rounded half even. - **`person-cut-total`**: the sum of pool cuts (`RespondWithPools`). A cut is pot × share ÷ total shares, rounded half even. People on hold today get no cut, and members outside their from/to dates are left out. - **`person-stated-total` / `-statement-count` / `-statement-date`**: see Statements below. - **`person-grade`**: the grade in force today. - **`person-retired`**, **`person-retired-from`**, holds, snapshots, `person-clashing`, `person-origin`: shown as stored. ## Sheet totals - `rollup-*`, `header-*`, `summary-*`, `month-*`, `tag-*` and `consolidated-*` are built from the same per-person figures. - The sheet's due total and overdue total are trimmed (`trimmedTotal`): with 3 or more people who have a figure, the single highest and lowest are dropped. - The claimed total and settled/open totals are not trimmed. Month and tag totals are not capped or trimmed. - The consolidated figures add up the descendant sheets' header figures. ## Which claims count - **`counts`** (both sides): OPEN or PENDING and not deferred, or SETTLED. - **`live`** also drops OPEN/PENDING claims that are not stated and either fall within one of the person's holds, or belong to a person whose retirement date today has reached (`retiredOn`/`retiredNow`). - DRAFT, VOID and DELETED claims never count. ## What gets frozen, and when - **Settle** freezes `settledDue`: the live due, with the late charge and floor already in it. - **Re-settle** (steward only) freezes it again at today's unbound due. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): - Binds each counting claim to its figure as a `statedDue` without the charge or floor, and unbinds the rest. - If the rate had ended, the claim is bound to n/a. - The `statedTotal` is the due total, capped. - It can be taken as of a past date, using the history tables. - PENDING claims, splitting (the remaining amount) and reassigning all unbind. Cancelling a statement unbinds everything. - **Closing or soft-closing a period** fixes the per-person and period totals (`PeriodClosing`). Reopening drops them. - **Changing the sheet's today** writes a SNAPSHOT of each person's due total, releases all edit locks, and auto-closes periods whose to-date plus `grace-days` is before the new today. ## Who may do what - **Roles** (`RoleStore`): clerk (the default), steward, viewer. An in-force delegation makes a user a steward. A viewer, or any change on an archived sheet, is refused by `refuseChange`. - **Permission matrix** (`perm-*` settings): the standing rule is that open, settle, void and close are allowed for clerk and steward; reassign and reopen for steward only. - **Steward only:** approve or reject a PENDING claim (rejecting needs a reason), void a SETTLED claim (only within 7 days of settling it), re-date, re-settle, merge, transfer, delegate. - **Clerk limit:** a clerk settling an OPEN claim whose due is above `clerk-limit` sends it to PENDING instead. - **Settling or approving is refused when:** - the user opened the claim or last edited it; - the claim is deferred; - the claim has no proof and its due is above the proof threshold (the grade's own threshold, else the sheet's, in force on the claim's date). - **Opening is refused when** the note is blank and the due is above `note-threshold`, or when the period's `cap` on OPEN/PENDING claims per person is already reached. - **Status moves:** only the moves allowed by `ClaimStatus.canBecome`. A DELETED claim can be restored only on the day it was deleted. Only DRAFTs can be edited. An editor's lock blocks other users. A claim with lines takes its amount from the lines. - **Voiding:** if the sheet has void reasons, a void needs one from the list. ## Dates, holds and closed periods - **Closed period:** any add, edit or status change to a claim whose `dueBy` (or would-be `dueBy`) falls in a closed period is refused. - **Soft-closed period:** the figures are fixed, but changes are still allowed. A claim added into one is flagged `lateEntry`. - **Retirement:** no claim may be dated after `retiredFrom`, or strictly inside a past retirement. Retired people cannot be merged or transferred. - **Hold:** only changes what counts (and pool cuts). It refuses nothing. - **Defer:** OPEN claims only, to a date after today. - **Split:** OPEN, not deferred, and the split-off amount must be less than the claim's amount. The new claim gets its own due-by and number. - **Blank claim date:** uses `entry-date` if set, else the sheet's today. ## Import, paste, quick add, plans - **People import:** each line is checked with `PersonRules`. A name that matches a person or alias updates that person, with the grade recorded from today. Anything else adds a person. If any line is bad, nothing is stored. - **Paste, plans and quick add** all go through the claim form's rules (`ClaimAdding.check`). - **Paste:** corrections are refused, and references must be unique. - **Plans:** dates the form refuses are skipped and retried on the next generate. - **Quick add:** creates a grade A person only after the claim passes its checks. - **Bulk settle** is all or nothing and writes `BATCH_SETTLED` with the frozen totals summed half up. Bulk open, re-date and reassign refuse claims one at a time. # 2. How hard it was to follow It was hard. The rules are well commented, but they're split across about 130 single-step classes wired together by YAML, plus about 40 front-end slots. The core due arithmetic (rate, rounding, compounding late charge, floor, cap, n/a, "counts") is written twice, once in Java (`Lateness`/`ClaimFigure`/`RollupService`/`TakeStatement`) and once in TypeScript (`rates.ts`/`overdue.ts`/`periods.ts`). A new developer would have to keep both copies in step by hand, and several figures shown on screen (settled/open, aged, backing, month and tag totals) exist only in the front-end copy.
